text: Should Indonesia be able to address safety and equipment-related concerns with regard to the management of the Flight Information Region (FIR) over the Riau Islands and the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) directs Indonesia to manage that FIR, what impact, if any, will this Page: 42 have on Singapore's position as an aviation hub?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the first place, the ICAO requires that the parties who are involved should satisfy themselves that, indeed, safety considerations can be fully met.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are many parties involved in our FIR, even though it is Singapore that is managing it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It will not be a simple issue to resolve, but we have to work together and the way in which we think is a positive direction for this subject to develop is towards ASEAN Seamless Sky, where we work together with one another to manage the airspace.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: One is on the issue of safety protocols.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I have asked about this in one of my cuts.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Could the Minister please clarify what are the routine obligations of LTA to check on the MRT operators' observance of safety protocols for maintenance and operations?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Second, I agree with the Minister that we should appreciate the hard work of MRT engineers and workers who are running our MRT system.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: They are having to cope with the situation caused by legacy issues, such as lack of timely maintenance and parts replacement in the earlier years and failure to provide timely capacity for increase in commutership, all of which can be attributed to the past leadership.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Three, a question for Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo: would the Ministry consider my suggestion of allowing a one-off opportunity for current owners of unauthorised e-bikes which can comply with the new criteria?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As I had stressed in my reply, I have been advised by legal counsel to be careful with what I say because investigations are still going on, so I cannot say too much.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is the SOP that covers all operators and that includes SMRT.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Then how come the safety procedure was breached in this instance?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Just to check, Mr Tan, are you asking for an amnesty and, if that is so, are you also suggesting that after the amnesty is granted, the e-bikes which do not meet the criteria continue to be allowed on the paths and on roads?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: No, I am not asking for an amnesty but I can foresee that under the new rules, perhaps, it is possible that some of the existing unauthorised e-bikes, because they were not the subject of application by their manufacturers to register for authorisation, but perhaps, these e-bikes can comply with the recommended protocols by the Panel.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, for these people, would it be possible that you can have a one-off opportunity for them to come forward to LTA to present their e-bikes for registration?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There must be a reason why those e-bikes were not authorised in the first place.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will Page: 43 have to consider the specific instances and take these on board when we draw up the implementation details for e-bike registration.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee: Mdm Chair, two clarifications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One, for Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo: earlier she mentioned about safety for budget airline crew and that there are independent studies and there are standards to follow.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But somehow or other, the crew themselves may not quite feel that these reports or studies gave them peace of mind.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, will the Ministry consider either publishing these reports or engaging the budget airline crew to assure them that these standards are adequate and that there is no excessive stress faced by them?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The passengers who take the flights will feel more comforted that the crew are well taken care of.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The second clarification is for Senior Minister of State Ng Chee Meng: he mentioned earlier that LTA will encourage taxi drivers and taxi operators to change their mindset with regard to third party private hire vehicles.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I was wondering if LTA themselves will be bold enough to also change their own mindset with regard to quality of service rules and taxi availability standards.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These proxy measures with regard to taxi service standards may, indeed, be obsolete in view of available technology and other measures of taxi services that commuter may want to experience today.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is always a plus and CAAS will follow up with him.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Just two points of clarifications to Senior Minister of State Mr Ng.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, if the vehicle population increases, of course, revenue can increase but the point of reference should be to keep it neutral to current revenue, since we want it to be mainly for easing congestion rather than raising revenue.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Second point is: what will the Ministry be doing to work with the taxi companies to ensure that there is a minimum fleet of taxis that can carry wheelchairs, given the expected increase that we will face in the future of elderly Singaporeans who are not ambulatory and will need to go to and from medical appointments more?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And also, to ensure that the fares are affordable for the most vulnerable group.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Given the vast amounts of things that we have to study, whether eventually there will be more or less revenue collected, it is too early to say.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Page: 44 On the second point on the composition of the taxi fleet, when the demand goes up, we will be encouraging the taxi fleet to answer to these needs.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As for the affordability part of it, MOT, together with MSF, has different programmes for the lower income groups to access certain grants so that they are able to afford such point-to-point services, should they need it.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: He said that any improper tweaking of the current COE scheme may result in an increase of the vehicle population and this contradicts the objective of the COE scheme.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: However, Madam, my proposal in asking for an adjustment to the existing Cat D is more towards making a proper and fairer allocation of quotas among the three different classes of motorcycles, according to the demand of the respective classes.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Hence, it does not increase the vehicle population.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, I do hope that the Ministry will further study this proposal.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I apologise if I got him wrong when he articulated the question.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And for the point on assistance to the lower-income, which I now recall the Member asked as well, can I suggest that we take a more targeted and needs-based approach towards assisting the lower income, outside of the COE system?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Because, ultimately, as I have said, the COE system is to allocate the scarce resource of vehicle needs for Singaporeans in a land-scarce Singapore.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, do you wish to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Further, on behalf of Members, I extend our appreciation to our officers from MOT and our Ministers for answering our questions, as well as sharing with us the future of transportation in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: On that note, Madam, I beg to withdraw my amendment.
